segments: full forty; and after [these] days the Sultan was summoned to enter.
And he mounted,
and before him all the princes [went] on foot.
And when he approached the gate of the palace of the Caliph,
for a time he stood while mounted;
and then the gate was opened for him,
and he entered the courtyard.
And the nobles of the Caliph came out to meet him,
and they lifted the veil (curtain);
and he entered the inner courtyard.
And they lifted again another veil;
and he entered and saw the Caliph sitting upon a throne raised about seven cubits from the ground,
and upon his head was a black turban,
and he was wrapped in a mantle that was likewise black.
For this the Banu Abbas (in Baghdad) wear and clothe [others] in,
unlike the Caliphs in Egypt, who wear and clothe [others] in white.
And in his hand was a golden scepter,
and on his two sides were two eunuchs.
And when the Sultan saw him,
he bowed down to the ground and prostrated several times.
And the Caliph commanded,
and they brought him up to another seat which was lower than his by about the height of a man.
And the Caliph said to the interpreter:
"Say to the Sultan:
'The Commander of the Faithful praises your zeal and commends your labors,
and is comforted by your approach,
and rejoices in you.
And lo, he has entrusted to you whatever God has entrusted to him of pastures and lands.
Therefore, fear God and execute justice in your domain,
and give thanks to the Lord for the sake of His favors toward you.'"
And the Sultan arose and bowed down to the ground and said:
"I am the servant and subject of your command,
and I rely upon God to help me accomplish your will."
And the Caliph commanded,
and they clothed the Sultan with seven black robes, one over the other,
and they placed a black, gold-embroidered turban upon his head,
and upon the turban a crown {or wreath} set with two precious ruby stones,
and upon each stone fifteen pearls of the finest quality,
and two golden bracelets on his wrists.
As for the golden collar, the Sultan was not willing to put it on his neck,
but it was placed in a dish (tray),
and a eunuch carried it before him.
And when he wished again to bow down to the ground,
it was not permitted to him,
because of the precious {OCR?} crown upon his head.
And the Caliph also gave him three purple banners with golden inscriptions,
and they were suspended on lances before him.
